title: Wren and the Room
premise: Urban explorer Dominic Lockridge and his small crew of documentarians descend into unmapped tunnels beneath a condemned mill town, where an excavation crew has just broken through a door sealed from the inside. The thing behind the door doesn't chase; it invites, rewriting memories so each survivor remembers welcoming it in, and the frost creeping up the walls records every name it takes. As the night stretches toward sunrise, Dominic must choose between destroying his recordings — the only proof of what was invited in and by whom — or using them to save the last survivors at the cost of exposing his own guilt. He burns the archive to break the invitation's hold, walks out at dawn with two others who no longer trust him, and leaves the truth buried with the door.
about_author: Kestrel Dunmore is the pen name of a former building surveyor who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned structures across the Rust Belt before turning to horror. Their fiction is known for claustrophobic settings and narrators whose meticulous record-keeping becomes both shield and confession.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He introduces his crew — Priya, Marcus, and teen tag-along Ellis — and his ritual of documenting everything as 'a kind of prayer.' A municipal survey shows nothing under the old Harrow Mill, but his own thermal drone disagrees. Emotional beat: obsessive purpose masking loneliness; he needs the tunnels to need him.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Dominic and Priya's POV alternating. They meet the excavation crew at the breach: a steel door, bolted from the inside, its hinges fused with frost in July. One worker, Ada Reyes, refuses to go near it. Emotional beat: dread of the wrongness — a seal implies something wanted to stay in, or keep something out.

chapters.title: What the Frost Writes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Inside the door, the walls bear frost patterns that resolve into names — including crew members not yet dead. Marcus films everything until his footage begins showing moments none of them remember living. Emotional beat: documentation curdles from comfort into evidence against them.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The entity doesn't attack; it offers. Each character hears a voice recalling a moment they 'let it in' — a kindness, a lie, a door held open. Ada reveals her grandfather helped seal the tunnel in 1954 and the sealing required a volunteer. Emotional beat: guilt made architectural.

chapters.title: Ellis Goes Missing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Ellis wanders off following frost patterns spelling his own name. The search fractures the group; Marcus insists on retrieving the footage cache instead. They find Ellis unharmed but serene, insisting he was never lost. Emotional beat: loyalty strains — who do you save first, the person or the proof?

chapters.title: Ada's Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV chapter. She explains the 1954 ritual: the thing beneath is fed by invitation, and the original sealers left one name on the door as bait — a Lockridge. Dominic realizes his family's surveying obsession is inheritance, not coincidence. Emotional beat: belonging revealed as a trap laid generations ago.

chapters.title: The Long Hour Before Sunrise
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Trapped by a collapse triggered by the entity, the survivors ration batteries and warmth while frost climbs their sleeves. Marcus, dying of cold, begs Dominic to transmit the footage out as a legacy. Emotional beat: the price of survival — some will pay it so others can carry the truth.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The entity shows him the full memory: his great-grandfather opened the door willingly, trading the town's prosperity for his family's line being forever 'welcome.' The frost finishes writing Dominic's name. Climactic beat: he understands the only way to refuse an invitation is to destroy the record that proves consent.

chapters.title: Burning the Archive
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax. He feeds every drive, notebook, and backup into a chemical flare, erasing the proof — and with it, the documented consent that anchors the invitation. The entity howls through Marcus's abandoned camera as the frost recedes. Emotional beat: sacrifice of identity; without the archive, who is Dominic?

chapters.title: Sunrise, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, resolution. Three walk out — Dominic, Priya, and a hollowed Ellis — into light no camera captures. Ada stays behind to reseal the breach with the excavation crew's explosives. Dominic can't remember why he came, only that he's glad to be going home. Final beat: survival purchased with truth, belonging rebuilt from absence.
